title: Venus May Be Tearing Itself Apart From Within
hook: Venus was long filed away as a geologically dead world. New 3D simulations say its giant rift valleys are young — and may still be pulling open.
key_points: Venus has enormous rift valleys, cracks where the crust is being stretched apart.
Advanced 3D simulations indicate some of those rifts formed relatively recently.
The models suggest the rifting could still be active and widening today.
That implies a far more restless interior than the 'dormant planet' picture allowed.
It challenges the long-held view of Venus as geologically dead.
content_html: Venus is Earth's near-twin in size and mass, and for decades it was treated as the dead twin — a scorched world whose geology had long since stalled. New work reported by ScienceDaily complicates that story. Using advanced three-dimensional simulations, scientists find that some of the planet's giant rift valleys, where the crust is being stretched and pulled apart, formed relatively recently and may still be expanding today.
extra_html: If the rifts are young and active, something inside Venus is still pushing. That points to a far more restless interior than the dormant-planet picture allowed, and it sharpens a question planetary scientists keep circling: why did two planets that started out so similar end up with such different geological fates? Venus has no Earth-style plate tectonics, so understanding what drives its deformation is a direct test of how rocky planets shed their internal heat. See the release for the modelling details.

related.title: Why Some Giant Planets Spin Faster Than 'Failed Stars'
related.hook: Astronomers clocked the spins of dozens of distant worlds and found a surprise: lightweight giant planets can twirl faster than the much heavier brown dwarfs — so mass isn't the whole story.

related.title: James Webb Reveals a Strange Atmosphere on a Hellish Lava Planet
related.hook: A planet so hot its surface is an ocean of molten rock turns out to have a real atmosphere — built from gases venting straight out of the lava itself, JWST finds.

related.title: A Tidally Locked Planet's Hidden Heat-Recycling Loop
related.hook: One side permanently roasting, the other frozen in endless dark — a lab model suggests this exoplanet's interior still evens things out with a steady loop of molten rock.

flashcards.prompt: What did the new 3D simulations of Venus suggest about its rift valleys?

choices.text: Some formed relatively recently and may still be widening
They are impact scars, not tectonic features
They all froze into place billions of years ago

flashcards.explanation_html: The simulations point to geologically young rifts that could still be actively opening — evidence of an interior that is far from dormant.

flashcards.prompt: Why does active rifting matter for how we think about Venus?
flashcards.back_html: It argues against the long-held picture of Venus as a geologically dead world, implying a much more active interior still driving deformation at the surface.
